author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Colombia is facing a severe drought in the northern Sucre region as the effects of El Nino leave farmers struggling to keep their cattle alive. The country’s cattle federation says more than 3,200 animals died in the Sucre area between June and late September, among roughly 19,000 deaths reported nationwide. Rancher Juan Pablo Correa says 143 cattle have died on the farms he manages despite efforts to find pasture and water. His attempts to grow maize for animal feed have also failed because of a lack of rain. Forecasters expect 70 to 80 percent less rain by the end of the year, raising fears that keeping cattle alive could become impossible. The government has announced support for cattle feed and irrigation and plans to postpone agricultural loan repayments, while questioning some industry loss figures. Some farmers say they are still waiting for assistance. Al Jazeera’s Alessandro Rampietti reports from San Pedro, Colombia.

description: New satellite images show the scale of destruction caused by Israel’s war on Gaza, with what remains of neighbourhoods visible from space. In some areas, the devastation stretches four kilometres and has increased during what is meant to be a ceasefire. In August, the UN Satellite Centre estimated that the number of destroyed structures had grown by 9 percent since a US-brokered truce nearly a year earlier. Comparisons between images from 2022 and now show entire sections of Rafah in southern Gaza have been erased. In Gaza City, much of the Islamic University of Gaza, once a cornerstone of education, has been reduced to rubble, with displaced families sheltering in tents. Gaza’s port, once the heart of its fishing industry, is also covered by rows of temporary shelters. Similar scenes are visible along much of the coastline, while Israeli attacks have forcibly displaced 1.9 million Palestinians. Israeli authorities said the attack targeted a commander of Hamas’s Qassam Brigades in northern Gaza, but the claim could not be independently verified. 
Rescuers took hours to reach the damaged building and recover those killed and wounded, with some children suffering severe burns. 
A funeral was due to be held for those killed, while Hamas had not immediately confirmed the reported killing of its commander. 
The attack comes as Palestinians in Gaza City continue to live under the threat of repeated Israeli strikes, many of which occur without warning. 
Residents say the attacks are making it increasingly difficult to carry out everyday activities and leaving people afraid to leave their homes.

“Iran has the capability of doing this … they have, clearly, the motivation. They’ve been attacking US and allied military facilities in the region for some time and have been expanding the scope of those attacks in terms of geography and strategic relevance for some time,” he said.

“So it doesn’t require a huge stretch of the imagination to write a scenario where Iran is a big player in this [the Fairford incident].”

However, Ereli said commentary on the incident at this stage was “speculation”.

Tehran denies any link to the incident.
